title: Vali's death and Tara's lament
hook: a widow runs toward the battlefield, and the winner wishes he'd lost

segments.voice: Yesterday: Vali's death and Tara's lament began, with an arrow from cover and the question he asked Rama: I wasn't fighting you. Did you state the other side's best argument? Day five hundred eighty-seven.

Word reaches the palace. The monkeys who saw it run back shouting: Vali is down. They want to run, or hide, or shut the gates against Rama. Tara doesn't. She was the one who warned him, earlier that same day, and he didn't listen. Now she runs the other way, out of the city, past the frightened crowd, toward the place where her husband is lying with an arrow in his chest. Her son Angada is with her.
screen: `VALI IS DOWN.` → `THE CROWD RUNS AWAY.` → `TARA RUNS TOWARD HIM.`

segments.voice: Tara reaches Vali and falls beside him. Her lament is long, and Valmiki gives it to her in full. She speaks to Vali: you lie on the bare earth as if you loved it more than me. She speaks to Sugriva, bitterly: now you have the kingdom. And she turns to Rama and asks him to kill her with the same arrow, so she can follow her husband. First idea: in the middle of an adventure story, the poem stops for a widow's grief, and lets it be angry. Tara isn't decoration. She warned Vali, and she was right. Second: Vali's last words. He speaks to Sugriva without anger now. Fate caught us both, he says, more or less. He asks him to care for Angada as his own son, and to listen to Tara, who understands things before anyone else does. He takes off the golden necklace that Indra once gave him and puts it on his brother. Then he dies. Third: Sugriva breaks. Now that he's won, he sees what winning cost. He says he would rather have his brother alive than the throne, and that he wants to die too. And Rama, the one who fired the arrow, is the one who has to steady them: he speaks to Tara, Sugriva and Angada about time, fate and duty, and tells them to perform the rites. Angada lights his father's pyre. Not long ago in the story, Rama gave a vulture a son's rites. Today Vali's own son gives them to his father, with the man who fired the arrow standing by.
screen: `TARA'S LAMENT, IN FULL.` · `VALI'S LAST WORDS TO SUGRIVA.` · `THE WINNER WISHES HE'D LOST.` · `ANGADA LIGHTS THE PYRE.`

segments.voice: Sit, and bring to mind a loss, large or small, yours or someone else's. Don't push it away, and don't dive into it either. Breathe in, and let the feeling be exactly its real size. Breathe out, and let your body hold it. Tara's grief wasn't tidy, and yours doesn't need to be. Just sit with it, steadily, breath by breath. The bell holds the time.
Tara. Vali's wise wife, mother of Angada, whose anger and grief fill today's lament after her husband falls.
Your line: fate caught us both. Today, let someone grieve or be angry without fixing it. Just listen. Day five hundred eighty-seven.

howItsDone: Tara is honored in Hindu tradition as one of the panchakanya, five women named in a verse some recite in the morning; Valmiki gives her lament for Vali several chapters.

original.note: Sanskrit tārā: star. Vali's wife, mother of Angada, known for her wisdom.

trapdoor: what you thought: Vali's death is the end of the episode.
what it means: the poem stays for the grief: Tara's, Sugriva's and Angada's.
what a scholar hears: Tara's laments run through Kishkindha 19–24; Vali's gift of the golden necklace is in Kishkindha 22; Tara is named in the panchakanya verse.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 19–24 (Tara's lament; Vali's last words; Sugriva's grief)
Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 25 (the funeral; Angada lights the pyre)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering and differ between editions; confirm against the edition the Keeper uses.
Tara's line about Vali lying on the earth as if he loved it more than her: paraphrased; confirm.
Tara asking Rama to kill her with the same arrow (Kishkindha 24): confirm.
The panchakanya verse (Ahalya, Draupadi, Kunti/Sita, Tara, Mandodari) has variants; howItsDone keeps it general.
